coverage: Read main.md, figures.md, supplement.md, supplement_figures.md, brief.md and for-agents.md in full at c6139d5 and inspected their linked figures. Checked disputed claims against the relevant ledger rows, value bindings, estimands and saved output tables. This was an internal consistency review. I did not rerun the analyses, rebuild the documents or independently recheck the cited publications. No files or Git state changed.

passage_a.quote: older dates for living land plants fit the fossil record if early plants were found several times less often, or became recognisable later.

items.verdict: The article supports the stated rate-or-delay trade-off for the vascular-plant ancestor. The brief extends it to the ancestor of all living land plants.
items.evidence: C48 models crown vascular bodies. C62 gives a separate interval-average requirement for bodies of any land plant, across a span already containing the Oman body fossil. C24 constrains delivered trilete encounter in one basin. The graphical abstract repeats the brief’s broader headline.

passage_a.quote: the ancestor of living *vascular* plants, which have internal plumbing, between about 452 and 428 Ma

items.verdict: The article and Figure 1b agree. The combined span of the three reported clock intervals is about 452–419 Ma.
items.evidence: Figure 1b shows 419 Ma as Morris et al.’s younger endpoint. The brief uses Hooper et al.’s 428 Ma endpoint for the combined span.

items.evidence: The quoted supplement sentence also says this holds for the crown record. In groups_shape.csv, the reviewed B2 steady-rate history has a passing age assignment in all four inclusion states, with best finite-sample p-values of 0.985–0.998.
